# core/jcs test data

Everything in this directory is committed fixture data, regenerated only
deliberately. Provenance of each file:

## `vectors/` — the RFC 8785 reference suite

Copied verbatim from the canonicalization reference implementation
maintained by the RFC 8785 author:
<https://github.com/cyberphone/json-canonicalization/tree/master/testdata>
at commit `master` (fetched 2026-08-29). Files: `input/*.json` →
canonical `output/*.json`, with the same expected output as hex bytes in
`outhex/*.txt`. The `weird.json` pair pins the UTF-16 property-name sort
order (a supplementary-plane key must sort before U+E000–U+FFFF) and the
minimal escape set.

## `es6-numbers.txt` — reference number vectors

Lines of `hex-ieee754,expected` where `hex-ieee754` is the 64-bit
IEEE 754 representation and `expected` is the exact ECMAScript
Number::toString serialization. Generated by the reference generator
shipped in the same repository (`testdata/numgen.js`, Apache-2.0,
retained here as `gen-es6-numbers.mjs` with only the line count and
output path changed) run under Node 22. The first 138 lines are the
static edge cases (±0, min/max subnormal, 2^53 boundaries, the 1e±21
cliffs, the RFC Appendix B values); the next 2000 are consecutive
subnormals; the rest are the generator's deterministic SHA-256-driven
random doubles.

## `rfc8785-appendixb.txt` — RFC Appendix B table

Transcribed from RFC 8785 Appendix B ("Number Serialization Samples"):
same `hex-ieee754,expected` format. The two table rows whose value is
NaN/Infinity (bit patterns `7ff...`/`7f8...`... i.e. `7fffffffffffffff`
and `7ff0000000000000`) are excluded — they are rejection cases, not
serialization cases, and covered as errors in the unit tests.

## `corpus.json` + `corpus-expected.txt` — independent-implementation corpus

Generated by `gen-corpus.mjs` (Node): a deterministic corpus of JSON
values — hostile keys (non-BMP vs U+E000–U+FFFF sort traps, controls,
escapes), nested containers, and number torture values — each
canonicalized by an ECMAScript reference canonicalizer
(recursively-key-sorted `JSON.stringify`, the construction RFC 8785
Appendix A itself uses). `corpus-expected.txt` is line N = canonical
bytes of corpus value N, hex-encoded so byte diffs are unambiguous.
The Go test replays corpus + expected with no Node involvement; rerun
`gen-corpus.mjs` after changing either file.
